Embalm {5}{W} ({5}{W}, Exile this card from your graveyard: Create a token that's a copy of it, except it's a white Zombie Angel with no mana cost. Embalm only as a sorcery.)
blocked_sentences: When this creature enters, you may exile target nonland permanent an opponent controls until this creature leaves the battlefield.
Embalm {5}{W} ({5}{W}, Exile this card from your graveyard: Create a token that's a copy of it, except it's a white Zombie Angel with no mana cost. Embalm only as a sorcery.)

needs.what: a persistent link recorded when a permanent exiles something -- on the exiler or on the exiled object -- naming which cards this source exiled, written by `exile` and readable by a later, separate resolution of a `leaves_battlefield` ability on the same source. Same one link Oblivion Ring, Banishing Light, Fiend Hunter and Angel of Sanctions all wait on; already filed on `data/authoring/gaps/oblivion_ring.json` under this exact capability slug
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `snapshot` is documented as the answer to last-known information, but it writes into `EffectContext.bindings`, which lives for exactly one resolution. The `self_enters` trigger that exiles and the `leaves_battlefield` trigger that would return are two separate abilities with two separate contexts, so a snapshot taken by the first is gone before the second runs. `exile` itself takes only `objects` and records nothing about who exiled what -- `zones.exile` just moves the object with `cause="exiled"` -- so once the Angel has left there is nothing anywhere saying which card in exile was hers. `delay` is the one op whose bindings are captured at scheduling time, but its `step` vocabulary is `upkeep`/`draw_step`/`begin_combat`/`end_step`, turn-based moments, not "when this permanent leaves".

needs.what: a selector key naming the cards exiled by the source permanent, e.g. `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}`, resolvable from a `leaves_battlefield` trigger after the source has already gone
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `SELECTOR_KEYS` in `src/automtg/engine/effects/selectors.py` has no exile-linkage key (`zone`, `controller`, types/subtypes/colors/keywords, p/t/mana_value comparisons, `exclude_self`, `self_only`, `count`, `chooser`, `random`, `target`, `binding`, `object_kind`, `name`, `damaged`). `{"target": "t1"}` only reaches targets of the ability currently resolving, and `{"binding": ...}` only reaches that resolution's bindings -- a `leaves_battlefield` trigger binds `subject`, `self` and `was_attacking`, none of which is the exiled card. The only selector that reaches exile at all is a plain `{"zone": "exile", ...}` filter, which matches every card in exile from every source, so returning over it would hand back cards the Angel never exiled. That is a different card, not an approximation of this one.

needs.what: an activated ability offered while its card sits in the GRAVEYARD -- `active_zones: ["graveyard"]` honoured for activated abilities, and `legality._activate_actions` scanning each player's graveyard for cards whose abilities declare it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `active_zones` exists in the schema and accepts `"graveyard"`, but `cards/loader.py:_compile_ability` only reads `model.active_zones` inside the *triggered* branch (line 360); an activated ability is hard-wired to `(Zone.BATTLEFIELD,)` at line 309, so declaring it is silently ignored. `engine/triggers.py:_candidate_abilities` likewise consults `active_zones` only for triggered abilities. `legality._activate_actions` iterates `state.battlefield` alone, so a graveyard card has no path to activation at all. The cost half is already there -- `Cost.exile_from_graveyard` is a real selector-shaped cost and `sorcery_speed_only` covers "Embalm only as a sorcery" -- which is exactly why this is one missing zone rather than a missing mechanic. The card-level alternatives (`retrace`, `suspend`, `kicker`) widen where a card may be *cast* from, never where an ability may be activated from.

needs.what: a token copy that applies an "except" clause -- `copy_permanent` (or a sibling) taking overrides for `colors`, added `subtypes` and a cleared `mana_cost`, and able to copy a card in a zone other than the battlefield
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `copy_permanent` creates a token whose `def_id` is the copied object's and takes only `objects`, `amount`, `controller`, `tapped` and `attacking` -- there is no way to say "except it's a white Zombie Angel with no mana cost", so the token would be a plain Angel copy with the printed colour, subtypes and cost. `create_token` cannot stand in either: it names a pre-declared token id checked by `validate_token_references`, and no white Zombie Angel copy of this card exists in the pool -- and a hand-declared 3/4 stand-in would not be a copy, so it would lose the enters trigger the real embalm token brings. `animate` sets base characteristics on an existing permanent and cannot create one.
